text: No open hi-hat. It answers notes 36, 38 and 42 only, so the open-hat hits AI Producer writes on note 46 are silent. Heard as missing off-beat hats in the house and techno drum clips.

fix.note: Note 46 plays the hat open, note 44 closed; a closed hit cuts off an open one.

text: At default settings a 0.5 input comes out at 0.96, almost double. A limiter that adds level by default is not safe to drop on a master, so it was left out of the mix.

fix.note: The ceiling now holds with Auto Makeup on, and the threshold defaults to 0 dB, so the plugin starts out transparent.

text: At default settings a 0.5 input peaks at 1.12, more than double. Loading it on a playing track would cause a jump in level.

fix.note: The dry and wet levels allow for the scaling inside JUCE's reverb. Mix at zero is the dry signal; the default is within 0.4 dB of the input.

text: No output level control. A separate SimpleGain was needed just to set its level in the mix.

fix.note: Output Level knob and parameter, -24 to +12 dB. The default of 0 dB leaves the sound as it was.

text: No output level control, and the default patch has its filter nearly closed (cutoff at 10% of range). A SimpleGain was needed to set its level.

fix.note: Output Level knob and parameter, -24 to +12 dB. The filter remark here was wrong: the default cutoff is 2000 Hz, not nearly closed. What is true is logged as its own entry.

text: The default patch has a slow attack with chorus and reverb on, which does not work for bass. Five settings had to be changed by hand. A few starting patches (bass, pad, lead) would save that.

fix.note: Four factory patches: Init, Bass, Pad and Lead, chosen from a Patch menu in the window or as host programs.

text: Live lists 49 AudioForge plugins but 61 are installed. Shakuhachi, Sitar and Classic Monosynth are among those missing from Live's browser. Six appear as 'AudioForge - Name' while the rest use the plain name.

fix.note: The four prefixed plugins now use plain names. Live lists 52 of the 60: the three named here appeared after a rescan. The eight it leaves out are the MIDI-only plugins, which Live does not host; that has its own entry.

text: The frozen sound holds about 13 dB below the level that was playing (RMS 0.08 against 0.35). With Phase Random above zero the phases come from the live input, not the frozen frame, which is the likely cause.

fix.note: A frozen 1 kHz tone now holds within 0.4 dB of the level that was playing, at 1000 Hz. It had also been 3% sharp, and the left channel was frozen onto both.

text: Its tone and level were chosen from the code's comments and preset names when the silence bug was fixed. Nobody has listened to it yet.

fix.note: This is the HiHat fix itself, waiting for a listen. Its level has since been calibrated (-9.6 dBFS) and is checked in CI; its tone is still untested by ear.

text: It recommends Operator, Analog and Wavetable, which Live Intro does not have, and cannot load instruments itself. It writes notes with a call Live has deprecated since version 11.

fix.note: It loads DrumSynth, BasicSynth, ElectricPiano and Polysynth itself, or the 909 Core Kit and Drift where those are missing, and writes notes with the current call. Run inside Live 12.4.6 Intro on 2026-10-05: all four loaded, BasicSynth came up on its Bass patch, and the clips held their notes.

text: Nothing in AudioForge does what Live's Utility did in the mix: gain, stereo width and mono in one device. SimpleGain and PanUtil each cover part of it.

fix.note: PanUtil now has gain and mono with its pan and width, and passes the signal unchanged at its default settings.

text: There is no AudioForge drum machine with a full house or techno kit (kick, snare, clap, closed and open hat). DrumSynth has three sounds; AnalogKick, SnareSynth, HiHat and TomSynth each need their own track.

fix.note: DrumSynth now has a clap on D#1, which with its kick, snare and two hats is the kit named here. AI Producer writes the clap into its house pattern.

text: Output levels differ by about 24 dB between AudioForge instruments in one mix. With every fader at 0 dB, on a house loop: DrumSynth peaked at +3.9 dBFS, ElectricPiano at 0.0 dBFS (after a 5 dB cut from SimpleGain, so about +5 on its own), BasicSynth at -14.3 dBFS and Polysynth at -19.8 dBFS (after a 7 dB cut, so about -13 on its own). The master peaked at +5.4 dBFS and clipped until the faders were set from measurements.

fix.note: Seventeen instruments calibrated so the loudest single note peaks at about -9 dBFS; checked in CI.

text: DrumSynth clips on its own at default settings: +3.9 dBFS peak on a four-on-the-floor pattern with snare and hats at velocities 70 to 100. It needed a 9.9 dB fader cut to sit at -6 dBFS.

fix.note: Output trimmed by 7.6 dB; the kick now peaks at -9 dBFS.

text: A measured mix was possible only with Live's Utility and Limiter and the mixer faders. The balance that worked on this loop, as peaks: drums -6, bass -9, chords -13, lead -15 dBFS, master -3 dBFS before a limiter with a -1 dB ceiling.

fix.note: The devices this needed now exist: PanUtil does what Live's Utility did, and the Limiter holds its ceiling (#26) with a working lookahead (#30). The balance recorded here stays as a reference.

text: After the instruments were calibrated to -9 dBFS, the same house loop peaked at -1.7 dBFS on the master with every fader at 0 dB, where it had clipped at +5.4. DrumSynth came in at -4.1 dBFS and ElectricPiano at -6.7.

fix.note: Kept as the reference for how much calibrated instruments add up to in a mix. Written into feedback/README.md under Levels. DrumSynth has since started following velocity (#34), which will bring its part of this down.

text: BasicSynth needs its fader at +5.7 dB to work as a bass in this mix. Its one patch was darkened by hand to make a bass (cutoff lowered, chorus and reverb off), which costs about 6 dB against its default level. It needs a bass patch of its own, at the calibrated level.

fix.note: The Bass patch peaks at -8.8 dBFS, the calibrated level, so it should need no fader boost. Not yet tried in the mix.

text: Adds 7.6 dB of peak level at default settings (noise in at -6 dBFS). Its own engine runs JUCE's reverb fully wet at three times its nominal level and mixes that in at 50%. It also allocates a buffer on every audio block.

fix.note: Now adds 1.0 dB of peak level at default settings. The reverb runs at its nominal level, and the buffer is no longer allocated on each block.

text: Takes 9.2 dB off the peak level at default settings, the largest drop of any effect. Loading it makes a track much quieter before anything is adjusted.

fix.note: The default threshold is -12 dB. A track at the calibrated level stays within 1 dB; the hotter check signal loses 3.2 dB, which is the compressor working.

text: Adds 3.9 dB of peak level at default settings.

fix.note: Now adds 0.7 dB at default settings. Tone fully open bypasses the tone filter, which had been moving the peaks.

text: Adds 3.0 dB of peak level at default settings, from its default makeup gain.

fix.note: No change in peak level at default settings. The default threshold is -12 dB, where the automatic makeup gain is zero.

text: Its built-in reverb sets the dry level to one minus the mix, the same mistake PlateReverb had, so its dry signal is doubled when the reverb mix is low. MelodyMaker has the same lines. Neither could be measured, because they wait for the host's transport.

fix.note: BassLine and MelodyMaker take their reverb levels from the same helper as PlateReverb. Not measured, for the reason given.

text: Lookahead does nothing. The read and write positions of its delay line are reset to the same place on every block, so there is no delay, and the gain is worked out from the current sample. It limits correctly, but with an instant attack and no lookahead it will distort on bass.

fix.note: The signal is delayed by the lookahead and the gain ramps down ahead of a peak. The delay is reported to the host as latency; the default is 5 ms.

text: The Filter Cutoff knob runs in a straight line from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, so everything below 2 kHz, where most of the useful sweep is, sits in the bottom tenth of its travel. The default of 2000 Hz shows as 10% of the range, which is what made the patch look nearly closed. The knob needs a skewed range. Check the other synths for the same thing.

fix.note: Polysynth and ClassicMonosynth have 1 kHz at the middle of the Cutoff knob. No other plugin had a frequency control on a straight line.

text: Nine instruments read a saved state without checking that it parsed: AcousticBass, BrassSection, ClassicMonosynth, ElectricPiano, Koto, Polysynth, Shakuhachi, Sitar and StringEnsemble. In setStateInformation only the first of three steps is inside the check, so a state the host hands over that is not valid would be read through a null pointer. Found by reading the code during review of PR 27; not reproduced.

fix.note: Reproduced as a crash, and found in nine more plugins under another variable name. All 18 now ignore a state that did not parse.

text: The Waveform control does nothing. The voice is handed the setting and ignores it, so every note is a sawtooth whatever the control says.

fix.note: Waveform now sets the oscillator. Its default moved from Sine to Sawtooth, so a new instance sounds as before.

text: Only 8 of its 18 settings are saved with a set. After Live was restarted, the AI Bass track had its chorus and reverb back at 0.30; both had been turned off for the mix. Filter type and saturation are lost the same way.

fix.note: Every setting and the chosen patch are saved. Sets saved in the old format still load, with chorus and reverb at their defaults as before, so the AI Bass track needs the Bass patch chosen once and the set saved again.

text: The plugin's window shows the default settings whatever the real ones are, so a reopened set looks reset when it is not. Its section labels and the filter type label are drawn under the knobs.

fix.note: The controls follow the settings, and the labels were moved clear of the knobs.

text: The Soft Clip shape has a step in it: the output falls from 1.0 to 0.5 as the input passes full scale, which would sound like harsh distortion as soon as the drive pushes a signal past it. Found while reading the code for the default level.

fix.note: The curve now bends over smoothly above full scale, towards 1.5.

text: It ignores velocity and timing. Every hit plays at full level, so the accents in a drum clip are lost, and every note in a block is triggered at the start of the block, up to 10 ms early at 512 samples. Found while adding the clap.

fix.note: A hit plays as hard as it is struck and starts at its own position. Clips with velocities under 127 now play quieter than before, so the drums in the house mix will want rebalancing.

text: Live does not list the eight MIDI-only plugins: ChordGenius, MIDI Arpeggiator, MIDI CC Mapper, MIDI Chord Generator, MIDI Groove Quantizer, MIDI Harmonizer, Macro Controller and XY Pad Controller. Live hosts plugins as instruments or audio effects only. To be usable there they would have to be rebuilt as instruments that send MIDI out, to be picked up by another track; that changes what kind of plugin they are in every host, so it needs a decision before any code.

At default settings SpectralFreeze takes 47.5 dB off the level of the test signal, which is close to silence, and GranularEngine takes 21.1 dB off. Neither has been looked into. PhaserFlanger takes 1.6 dB off, the only other effect outside 1.5 dB apart from VintageCompressor, whose 3.2 dB is it compressing.

fix.note: SpectralFreeze passes a tone through at 0.0 dB and holds a frozen one at 0.0 dB; it had the three faults FreezeFX had. GranularEngine and PhaserFlanger are carried on in their own entry.

text: Small things seen in passing and left: PanUtil's stereo-field circle is drawn behind its Width slider, and in DrumSynth a soft closed hat after a loud open one steps the ringing open hat down, because the hat has one level for both.

At default settings GranularEngine takes 21.1 dB off the level of the test signal. Not yet looked into; a granular effect that is fully wet with sparse grains may be meant to be quiet. PhaserFlanger takes 1.6 dB off. Separately, OrganEmulator, PadSynth and WavetableSynth use M_PI, which Microsoft's compiler does not define, as DrumSynth did. Whether they fail to compile on Windows has not been checked: CI builds plugins on Linux only.

The generated bass plays one note for the whole track: 288 notes, all A1, over 72 bars. The script's README says the bass follows the chord progression, and the chords clip does move (seven different pitches). Seen when reading the clips back from Live after a house track was generated.

fix.note: The bass now plays each bar's chord root, from the same progression the chords clip uses. Techno's i-i-i-i still holds one note by design.

text: Importing the four stems of one song into a Live Set left them out of line. Live warped each to its own tempo guess (150, 150, 74 and 74 BPM for a 148 BPM song) and moved each clip's start to its guessed first beat, up to 1.46 s in. The script could not see or change a clip's warping or markers. Copies of those clips made on the timeline also came out the wrong length. Seen while setting up the Cloud9 show.

fix.note: The script can now describe a clip, switch its warping and move its start and end. For the stems themselves the fix was switching Live's Auto-Warp Long Samples setting off before importing.

text: The Fall-off articulation drops the note at the wrong time and stays there. Rendered on F#4 (trumpet, section of 4, note held 2.5 s): the pitch starts falling 0.5 s after note-on, reaches E4 (about 10%, two semitones) by 0.8 s, and then holds E4 for the rest of the note. A fall-off is expected at the end of a note (on release), dropping further and fading. Code: BrassEngine.cpp, case Articulation::FallOff, counts from samplesSinceNoteOn. Found while scoring the half-time transition of the Cloud9 show; the fall there was done by hand instead.
